The kit is now part of ParleyPort. It lives in the same Go module and carries ParleyPort's version, so one tag covers the server, the kit and the `fortress` and `notify` helpers.

**Adopting apps:**

- **Moving up:** replace `require github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport/kit vX` with `require github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport v1.3.4` in every `go.mod` that names the kit, also a `// indirect` line in a module such as `desktop/`, and run `go mod tidy`. The import paths stay `github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport/kit/...`, so no Go file changes.
- **Still on the old module:** `kit/v1.2.0` is the last version of `github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport/kit`. It holds no packages and brings ParleyPort 1.3.4 along, so an app that only bumps the kit keeps building.
- **Taking a pinned password:** an app that reads the owner's password hash from its environment hands it to `signin.Config.PinnedPassword` instead of wrapping the store.
- **Plugins:** nothing to do. The helpers stay attached to every release under the same names.

## ✨ Added

- **An operator can pin the owner's password from outside**, such as from an environment variable. `signin.Config.PinnedPassword` takes its hash, from `signin.HashPinned` or in the app's own form with a `Check` of its own. While it is set it is the owner's only password and closes an open app. Changing, removing or resetting it answers `pinned`, `options` and `me` say `pinned` so the page offers no reset, and a new hash ends the owner's sessions. `signintest.Run` checks all of this with `Options.Pinned`.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The kit's relay says in its log why a connection ended**, as ParleyPort's server does: a newer connection with the same ID, a device that hung up, a stalled line, a full queue, a refused hello or a key the relay no longer serves. The relay key shows up only as a short fingerprint, and the instance ID is cut short.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **go-jose 4.1.9 for the sign-in services.** `signin` checks keys and tokens from a sign-in service with go-jose, and versions before 4.1.6 could be made to panic or stall on a crafted key set. Apps with `signin` should move up.
- **gorilla/websocket with a strong mask key.** The MQTT client in `mqttha` came with gorilla/websocket 1.5.3, which masks its frames with a weak random source (GO-2026-6278). The kit takes the commit that fixes it, since there is no release with the fix yet.
